messages:
carla_support: FYI — Acme reporting a sudden surge of 502s and timeouts starting ~08:12 UTC. They sent a cURL repro and say errors started after they increased request concurrency. Opening thread to coordinate. @raj @alice
raj: Oncall here, looking at metrics. I see a spike in 502/503s and a big jump in open connections on eu-edge-hostpool-3 around 08:09. Pulling traces now.
alice: Seeing SYN_RECV backlog and increased accept queue drops on the edge. Is this isolated to Acme or multi-tenant? @sam_dev can you check request headers and request IDs?
sam_dev: Trace sample (request-id: r-0a1b2c): gateway returns 502 with upstream error 'broken pipe', then runtime returning 504 for some long-polls. I'm starting a pcap on the edge gateway.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: no deploys between 07:30-08:30 UTC for eu-west clusters.
carla_support: Customer-provided repro: ```curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' -H 'X-Requested-Concurrency: 40' -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate``` They say they ramped concurrency from 8->40 at 08:10.
raj: Noted. I see rolling restarts for runtime-worker@eu-west around 08:08-08:11 — looks like nodes were removed then re-added (autoscaler?). That could explain connection resets and the pool churn. Who kicked an autoscale event?
alice: No manual rollout. Checking cluster autoscaler logs now. Early signal: several short-lived node terminations due to OOM-kills around 08:07; autoscaler started replacing nodes which caused backend socket churn.
sam_dev: From gateway logs: `ERROR write tcp 10.0.4.21:443->10.0.8.7:56322: write: connection reset by peer` repeated across many upstreams. Also seeing TCP FIN flood from runtime nodes.
carla_support: Quick mitigation options: 1) bump gateway connection pool size and idle timeouts to reduce churn impact, 2) route Acme to a less impacted pool / fallback model variant, 3) ask Acme to throttle concurrency while we stabilize. Which to do now?
raj: I'll apply option 1 immediately and watch. Pushing temporary config: `gateway.max_conns: 2000 -> 4000`, `gateway.idle_timeout: 30s -> 60s`. Applying to eu-west edge now.
alice: Applying infra changes to edge config and increasing connection limits on the gateway fleet. Also enabling more conservative draining on autoscaler so we don't evict active connections abruptly.
sam_dev: Confirming capture — error rate on Acme's endpoint dropped from ~38% to ~6% within 90s of config change. Traces show fewer 'broken pipe' errors and shorter retry cascades.
carla_support: On the customer call now — they confirmed errors dropped and will keep concurrency at 16 for the next hour while we follow up. They asked for root cause and timeline.
raj: Immediate action items: (1) postmortem + timeline for infra (alice) (2) implement circuit-breaker/soft-drain for runtime restarts (raj) (3) harden autoscaler drain logic and avoid OOM-induced terminations (raj + infra) (4) customer KB update for recommended concurrency ramp patterns (carla_support). I'll own #2 and coordinate with infra on #3.
alice: I'll gather logs, deployment/autoscaler events, and node OOM traces and start the postmortem doc. Linking to working doc: https://redwood.internal/postmortems/3791234567 (internal).
carla_support: Creating a follow-up ticket for the customer KB and client-side best practices. Will send a short writeup to Acme engineering and schedule a 14:00 UTC postmortem check-in tomorrow.
incident-bot: incident-bot: incident 3791234567 marked mitigated (P1 -> monitoring).
oncall-bot: oncall-bot: closing handoff channel, please file follow-ups in JIRA.
raj: Thanks all — leaving follow-ups in the infra and runtime queues. If errors recur I'll reopen.
carla_support: Customer is satisfied with the workaround for now. We'll monitor metrics for the next 24h and schedule the postmortem. :thumbsup:
